item.title: Xi meets Trump, calling for continued efforts to steer China-U.S. relations on right course
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with U.S. President Donald Trump, who is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday in Shenzhen, calling for continued efforts to jointly steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relations in the right direction toward the future. Trump is in the southern Chinese city for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. During the meeting, Xi said that China-U.S. relations have generally maintained a stable and positive trajectory, bringing tangible benefits to people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world. Xi said that he and Trump had jointly explored the right way for China and the United States, as two major countries, to get along, established a new positioning of a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability and given it new meaning based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. The new positioning has been welcomed by the people of both China and the United States, as well as by the international community, he added. Xi stressed that building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented and pioneering endeavor, adding that the key to sustaining the current positive momentum lies in taking concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state. The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. Xi called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns, and work toward mutual benefit. The cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, the repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness, and reciprocity. China and the United States should strengthen communication and coordination to guard against safety risks of artificial intelligence (AI) and ensure that AI always remains under human control, he said. On the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should do the right thing and avoid major disruptions to China-U.S. relations, Xi said. Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of U.S.-China relations, and both sides should maintain the positive momentum of the stable development in bilateral relations. The United States does not support "Taiwan independence," Trump said. item.title: China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- The following is the full text of the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, released on Thursday. China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace Xi Jinping, President of the People's Republic of China, Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation, and Donald J. Trump, President of the United States of America, met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. The Russian and U.S. heads of state expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic trilateral Summit. The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security. 1. As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, China, Russia, and the United States committed to reform the U.N. so that the U.N. can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security. 2. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. 3. The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. 4. The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping chairs the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and delivers important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam. item.title: Xi says China-Russia relations bring stability, certainty to turbulent world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye) SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Wednesday that China-Russia relations have brought greater stability and certainty to a world of turbulence and transformation. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that this year marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. He said that China-Russia ties set an example for a new model of major-country relations featuring equality, mutual respect, good faith, and win-win cooperation. Xi called on both countries to deepen all-round cooperation and firmly uphold the due responsibilities and obligations of major countries to guide and promote a multipolar world and democratization of international relations. Both sides should leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between their governments, legislatures, militaries and political parties to ensure that the consensus reached by the two heads of state is effectively implemented, Xi said. Xi called on the two countries to provide a more stable and predictable investment and business environment and protect the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises from both countries. The development of China and Russia is closely intertwined with that of the Asia-Pacific region, and APEC is an important platform for enhancing cooperation, Xi noted. China stands ready to work with the Asia-Pacific family, including Russia, to chart a course for the region's prosperity and development and build an Asia-Pacific community together, Xi said. Putin said he and Xi have held four productive meetings so far this year, helping sustain the sound development momentum in Russia-China relations. High-level exchanges have been close, bilateral trade has reached a new high, and practical cooperation has made substantial progress across various fields, he said. Russia is willing to strengthen back-to-back strategic coordination with China, expand cooperation in trade, energy, education and other fields, and broaden cultural and people-to-people exchanges to better benefit the two peoples, Putin said. Russia also stands ready to work with China to promote development and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, advance the process toward a multipolar world and build a more just and equitable global governance system, he added. item.title: Xi calls for jointly building Asia-Pacific community to prosper together
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Tao) SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged on Wednesday that China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all. Addressing the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in the southern metropolis of Shenzhen, Xi called on business communities in the region to uphold the entrepreneurial spirit and make greater contributions to economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. Under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the two-day summit has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland. "The Asia-Pacific is our home; it is here we jointly pursue development and cooperation," Xi said. Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has been one of the world's most dynamic engines of growth. Today, the APEC economies are home to about 40 percent of the world's population, and account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of global trade. As the world becomes more turbulent and the global economy lacks growth momentum, the Chinese president said the region must answer the "hard questions of our times": to open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways? In his response, Xi put forward proposals on how the region can prosper together, calling on APEC economies to uphold peace and stability, build bridges of opening up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth and expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. All parties in the region must "uphold the postwar international order," he said, calling on them to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation and address challenges through solidarity and coordination. Xi said the Asia-Pacific should support free and open trade and investment while keeping the global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. "History tells us that opening doors brings progress while closing doors leaves one behind," he said, calling for efforts to steadily advance the process of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. He stressed the need to forge partnerships in science, technology and innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and promote green and low-carbon development. "By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific," the president said. The region should also remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy, and promote development that is balanced and delivers benefits to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness, Xi said. According to Xi, there is much to draw from the success of Shenzhen, host of this year's APEC CEO Summit and the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. Over the past 40 years and more, Shenzhen has been a pioneer in China's pursuit of reform and opening up. It has achieved a historic transformation from a small border town into an international metropolis, creating a miracle in the history of global development, Xi said. Noting that the Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects, Xi said China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world. "This will help us explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific," he said. Looking ahead, as China's ties with the Asia-Pacific grow increasingly close, Xi said China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. The development blueprint is "an invitation for cooperation China has sent to business communities from around the world," he said. Xi said China will provide the global business community with a super-sized open market, a promising land for development, as well as an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation. He highlighted China's accelerating efforts to develop a big, open market and build a modern industrial system, pledging a more stable and predictable first-class environment for companies from around the world to invest and do business in China. Calling the Asia-Pacific business communities "pioneers of the global economy," he said they are "more than welcome to continue to get actively involved in China's reform and opening up and modernization drive, and share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization." Leaders of APEC economies, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, attended the summit. Having previously hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meetings in 2001 and 2014, China is taking on the role of APEC host for the third time this year. It has hosted more than 300 APEC meetings and events this year and reached nearly 50 practical outcomes with other APEC economies in the economic and trade field. item.title: Shenzhen summit marks first face-to-face meeting among Chinese, Russian, U.S. heads of state in history
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- The meeting of the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state in south China's Shenzhen will be the first face-to-face meeting in history involving the top leaders of the three countries, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Monday. Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Nov. 19, according to the ministry. Mao said the heads of state will have an in-depth exchange of views on maintaining world peace and promoting strategic stability in major country relations, which is of groundbreaking significance. Noting that China, Russia and the United States are all founding members of the UN and permanent members of the UN Security Council, Mao said the three countries have fought together to achieve the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War. Under current circumstances, the three countries shoulder the important responsibility of cooperating to address global challenges and promote world peace and stability, said Mao. Strengthening communication, managing and controlling differences, and stabilizing relations among China, Russia and the United States serve the interests of the three countries, meet the expectations of the international community, and are conducive to stabilizing the world situation and promoting dialogue and cooperation, she said.
